    ⚔️ Cubra Faith¶

    "The way needs no ornament. It needs walking."

    Cubra Faith is the plain Kirivs-bin as practiced by the Cubra Tribe — the demon tribe on Yak Island southwest of Estran and below the Asatru-controlled territory, across the sea from the Koebi Tribe. Where every other Demon Continent and Yak Island people has accented the bin into a sect, the Cubra have not. Their faith is Kirivs-bin without addition, without priesthood, without shrine — the control sample that proves the bin still walks as it was.

    Origins¶

    The Cubra demons are of the main demon race — like the Asatru Empire and Maomodor Kingdom — and their island settlement dates to the general demon dispersal after the Demonic War. Unlike the Koebi (green, meditative), the Malgardians (purple, lineage-pure), or the Mountain Tribe diablos (winged, nocturnal), the Cubra crossed no distinctive biological or historical threshold that demanded a new theology.

    When the demon diaspora produced Malgardism, Padamalgardism, Farsightism, Tolumin, Demonism, and Gedarism's outright rejection, Cubra elders are recorded as having listened politely and then said: "We have a way. It still works."

    There is no prophet, no date, no text. Cubra Faith is Kirivs-bin, and Kirivs-bin predates Kirivis himself, stretching to the earliest demon tribes of Age 2.

    Beliefs¶

    • Legends are the scripture — Cubra young learn the stories of Kirivis and the ancient warrior-kings as Asatru young do: not as gods but as examples to emulate.
    • Kirivis is the last great legend — the Demon King who saw the Hybrian conspiracy, waged the 45-year war (599–554 BGD), and died revealing the truth. His sacrifice is the highest lesson; Cubra add no other figure.
    • Action is prayer — every battle, craft, self-improvement, fishing run between islands is a step on the path. There are no Cubra temples, no priests, no sacred texts beyond the legends themselves.
    • Honor is earned, not inherited — worth is what you have done, not who your parents were. Cubra honor duels follow the plain Asatru form: challenge as recognition of worth, resolution by duel ideally to first blood.
    • Comfort is the enemy — Cubra live simply. Their island longhouses are sturdy but unadorned; surplus is not hoarded. Asceticism is clarity.
    • No sectarian claim — the Cubra explicitly deny that plainness is superiority. "We are not the true bin because we added nothing. We are simply the bin that stayed still while others walked ahead. They may be further along. We keep the path behind them clear."

    Practices¶

    • Legend-study (plain) — communal telling around hearths, without the Tita Commentary or the Ledger of the Far Sight
    • Honor duels (plain) — standard demonic form; no wooden staves, no wargames, no night-shift mediation — steel, respect, yield
    • Ascetic living — no palaces, no hoarded wealth
    • Family lineage — dying without passing knowledge to the next generation is dying incompletely; Cubra households keep lineage recitation but without Malgardist purification rites
    • Hospitality to sects — Cubra settlements are known as neutral ground where Malgardist priests, Kutra Ledger-keepers, Koebi masons, and Mountain Demonists can meet without conceding precedence, precisely because the hosts claim no sectarian ground to cede

    Relation to Kirivs-bin¶

    Identity — not a sect.

    Cubra Faith is Kirivs-bin under another name, the way a still pond is the same water as a river. Maomodor Kingdom shares this plain adherence on a far larger scale; together Cubra and Maomodor are the Demon's Continent's reminder that the bin does not require elaboration to survive.

    • The Asatru Empire recognizes Cubra practice as fully orthodox bin (and occasionally sends young Asatru officers to Cubra for "plain bin training")
    • Sectarian theologians cite Cubra precisely because it cannot be accused of sectional bias: when Malgardists and Padamalgardists dispute shore-priest ordination, they agree to let a Cubra elder judge — and do
    • Cubra demons can and do walk the Demonist night market in the Mountain Tribe or stand vigil on the Bloodcoast without theological friction: the plain bin is compatible with all its sects, because it contains them all potentially

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Cubra Tribe — universal among Yak Island demons; estimated ~95%+ plain bin observance, remainder syncretic but not separately organized
    • Exemplary: Maomodor Kingdom — the much larger plain-bin polity on the mainland (see below) recognizes Cubra as kin; the two exchange envoys styled "keepers of the same way in different weather"
    • Diplomatic: Yak Island's required neutral ground — every island faith trusts Cubra to host without preaching
    • Continental mirror: Asatru scholars use Cubra and Maomodor together to map what bin looks like without local accent — the baseline against which every sect's addition becomes visible

    Maomodor — the larger plain bin¶

    The Maomodor Kingdom (southwest of Blazeyard, below the Kutra Tribe) is the Demon Continent's other great plain-bin nation — and its largest by population. Like Cubra, Maomodor is of the main demon race but, distinctively, highly multi-racial: its "shared demonic nationality" means populations of every type walk freely everywhere, and many races live permanently within its borders.

    Maomodor's plain adherence is therefore more politically consequential than Cubra's: it demonstrates that the bin need not be tribal to be orthodox. Maomodor demons study the same legends, fight the same honor duels, practice the same asceticism — and extend them casually to whichever neighbor shares the street, whatever their species.

    See: Kirivs-bin, Maomodor Kingdom
